newsitem.title: USA: Texaco says settles racial bias suit.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says settles racial bias suit.

text.p: Texaco Inc said on Friday it had reached an agreement in principle to settle the class action lawsuit filed against it by about 1,400 black employees in 1994.

The company said it had agreed to pay the plaintiff-class $115 million, along with a one-time salary increase of about 11 percent for current employees of the plaintiff-class, effective January 1, 1997.

The company also said it agreed to create an "Equality and Tolerance Task Force" to determine potential improvements to the company's human resources programs, as well as to monitor the progress being made in those programs.

Three members of the task force will be appointed by the plaintiffs, three members by Texaco and there will be a mutually agreed chairperson, Texaco said. Texaco also will implement diversity, sensitivity and mentoring programs.
It would consider nationwide job postings of more senior positions than are currently posted.
The racial discrimination suit charged the oil giant with systematically discriminating against blacks and denying promotions.
